surprise.title: Your Half Moon Cay beach day is on an island presidents fished and a cruise line bought for $6 million
surprise.body: RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay is the Bahamas' Little San Salvador Island, about 100 miles southeast of Nassau, halfway between Eleuthera and Cat Island. Franklin Roosevelt fished its waters in 1935 and came back to swim in 1936, and Dwight Eisenhower trolled there in 1957. Norwegian Cruise Line bought it next, and the SS Norway brought the first big ship on May 30, 1980. In 1987 someone proposed filling its lagoon with New York trash to build condos on top, and the Bahamas said no. Holland America bought the island in December 1996 for $6 million and opened it as Half Moon Cay in December 1997. Only about 50 of its 2,400 acres are developed, so the rest stays a nesting ground for seabirds. This year Carnival added a new pier, so you walk straight off the ship instead of riding a tender boat. Your day there is a true $0 day: the beach, loungers, umbrellas, tram and BBQ lunch are all included, so just remember to bring a ship towel. Back home today runs about 51 to 62 degrees under clouds with a 56% chance of rain, and sunset is at 5:36 PM. Eighteen days until you sail on December 13.
